title: Class PhyloMArrayLM — PhyloMArrayLM-class
text: PhyloMArrayLM objects contain slots (apart .Data) contain list components MArrayLM-class. addition, contain following tree-specific components: phy: phylogenetic tree used regression, class phylo. modelphy: phylogenetic model trait evolution, argument call phylolmFit. measurement_error: Boolean, TRUE additional measurement error, argument call phylolmFit. phy_trans: List transformed phylogenetic trees obtained fit using phylolm gene. optpar: Vector optpar obtained fit using phylolm gene. lambda_error: Vector lambda_error parameters obtained fit using phylolm gene. sigma2_phy: Vector phylogenetic sigma2 parameters obtained fit using phylolm gene. sigma2_error: Vector sigma2_error parameters obtained fit using phylolm gene.

title: Get Bounds on alpha — getBoundsSelectionStrength
text: functions tries find reasonable bounds \(\alpha\) parameter OU process using scaled phylogenetic half-life \(t_{1/2} = \log(2) / \alpha / h\), \(h\) total height tree. \(t_{1/2} = D)\), means trait need time \(D \times h\) cover half distance optimal value (see Hansen, 1997). Small values \(D\) means high selection pressure (large \(\alpha\)), large values \(D\) means low selection pressure (small \(\alpha\)). default maximum value \(D\) relative_half_life_max = 10000 (selection week process looks like BM). default minimum value \(D\) relative_half_life_min = 0.0001 (selection strong tips weakly correlated). function makes sure maximum \(\alpha\) value associated relative_half_life_min lead underflow errors rescaling tree.

title: Get Bounds on alpha — getBoundsSelectionStrength
text: Hansen, T. F. (1997). Stabilizing Selection Comparative Analysis Adaptation. Evolution, 51(5) :1341.

title: Phylogenetic Comparative Method using LIMMA — phylolmFit
code: ## Simulate a tree set.seed(1289) ntips <- 20 tree <- ape::rphylo(ntips, 0.1, 0) condition <- sample(c(0, 1), ntips, replace = TRUE)  ## Simulate data with replicates reps <- sample(1:5, ntips, replace = TRUE) rep_ids <- make.unique(rep(tree$tip.label, times = reps), sep = "_") ngenes <- 20 dat <- matrix(rnorm(sum(reps) * ngenes, 1, 0.5), nrow = ngenes) rownames(dat) <- paste0("g", 1:ngenes) colnames(dat) <- rep_ids  ## Add differentially expressed genes condition_reps <- rep(condition, times = reps) ndiff <- 5 dat[1:ndiff, ] <- dat[1:ndiff, ] + rexp(ndiff, 1/2) %*% t(condition_reps)  ## Design matrix design <- cbind(rep(1, ncol(dat)), condition_reps) colnames(design) <- c("(Intercept)", "condition") rownames(design) <- rep_ids  ## linear model fit pfit <- phylolmFit(dat,                    design = design,                    phy = tree,                    model = "OUfixedRoot",                    measurement_error = TRUE,                    use_consensus = TRUE) #> Loading required package: ape  ## eBayes correction pfit <- eBayes(pfit, trend = TRUE) limma::topTable(pfit, coef = 2) #>          logFC   AveExpr          t       P.Value     adj.P.Val           B #> g2  25.2948752 7.6462148 194.650854  0.000000e+00  0.000000e+00 1190.049817 #> g5   9.0026076 3.1593224  72.724947 1.262101e-293 1.262101e-292  661.316179 #> g4   7.7178819 2.6802085  62.294317 4.560948e-259 3.040632e-258  582.396074 #> g1   0.7354200 0.7938382   5.525255  4.975259e-08  2.487629e-07    6.885335 #> g3   0.6213833 0.6894336   4.654513  4.028371e-06  1.611348e-05    2.641743 #> g15  0.1925638 0.6160945   1.446090  1.486921e-01  4.956405e-01   -6.955053 #> g6  -0.1761358 0.5960219  -1.330530  1.838666e-01  5.253331e-01   -7.115052 #> g20  0.1474773 0.6529736   1.126593  2.603806e-01  5.422614e-01   -7.365100 #> g18  0.1405957 0.5648386   1.057823  2.905765e-01  5.422614e-01   -7.440103 #> g13 -0.1391035 0.5997454  -1.048037  2.950581e-01  5.422614e-01   -7.450394

Compute 1 - rho — rho_prime
text: rhoprime = 1 - rho = (1 - exp(-2*alpha*t_H)) / (2 * alpha * t_H) variance OU variance BM. Taken Cornuault, 2023, Syst. Biol. fraction variance can explained "neutral" BM evolution. alpha goes 0, rhoprime goes 1: trait can explained "neutral" BM process. alpha goes Inf, rhoprime goes 0: trait deterministic.
